# Design notes

Why the code is shaped the way it is.

None of this is needed to *use* the tool — [README.md](README.md) and
[SETUP.md](SETUP.md) cover that. This is for anyone modifying the scripts, and
it exists mainly to stop a plausible-looking change from quietly breaking
something.

---

## Why the Form is generated by a script

The workbook addresses the response tab **by column position**. One question
added, removed or reordered shifts every column and silently breaks every
formula that reads it.

Generating the Form from the same CSV that builds the workbook is what
guarantees the two agree. It also means a change to the spell list is one re-run
rather than nine re-pastes into the Forms UI.

`verify_form_script.js` executes the generated `.gs` against a mock `FormApp`
and asserts that the question order matches the columns the workbook reads
(C=Player … R=Other), that the per-level choice counts match the CSV, and that
the email and editing settings are right.

## Never write a plain reference into the response tab

Google Forms **inserts** a row per response rather than filling the next blank
one, and the insert lands exactly where a plain reference points.
`'Form Responses'!D2` becomes `D3` after one response, `D4` after two. The
workbook then reads blank rather than wrong, which is a slow way to notice.

Every reference into the response tab is therefore a **bounded `INDEX`**:

```
INDEX('Form Responses'!$D$1:$D$200, 2)
```

Row insertion extends the range's end and leaves the literal row index alone.
`verify_workbook.py` scans the built workbook and **fails** if a plain row
reference reappears, so this cannot regress unnoticed.

Whole-column `$D:$D` would be equally safe, but makes the offline formula
evaluator crawl a million rows per reference — hence the bound. 200 rows is
headroom for a 24-wizard roster.

## Why the response tab must be repointed, never renamed

Linking a Form to an existing spreadsheet always creates a new tab
(`Form Responses 1`); it will never write into one the workbook shipped. The
formulas have to be repointed at Google's tab with a find-and-replace, and the
placeholder deleted **afterwards**.

Deleting first turns every reference into `#REF!` permanently — recreating a
sheet by the same name does not heal them. SETUP.md gives the sequence.

---

## Where the spell list comes from

**Primary source: `TheMasterSpellbook/`** — saved pages from D&D Beyond's
`/spells` listing, filtered to **Class = Wizard** and the 15 Forgotten
Realms-legal sources. 21 pages, 20 rows each.

The wizard filter is the whole trick: the listing rows carry no class, so
filtering makes class attribution implicit and nothing has to be expanded or
guessed.

Two things the saved rows do **not** contain:

- **Class** — solved by the filter, as above.
- **Source book** — the badge at the bottom-right of each card is rendered
  client-side, so `Ctrl+S` never captures it. Source is joined by spell name
  from a local directory of D&D Beyond book exports instead.

Cantrips are dropped throughout: they are not kept in a spellbook.

### Re-scraping the listing

Apply Class = Wizard in D&D Beyond's own filter UI — don't hand-edit the query
string, because the page exposes two class-id schemes (`2190886` and `8`) — then
save each page into `TheMasterSpellbook/`.

Filenames don't matter: the extractor globs `*.htm` and dedupes on `data-slug`,
so overlapping saves are harmless. It reads the advertised page count from the
pagination and warns loudly if pages are missing, so a truncated scrape cannot
silently shrink the list.

## Parsing the book exports

Six things that will bite anyone touching `extract_spells.py` or
`crosscheck_books.py`.

**Find class lists by anchor id, never by heading text.** Xanathar's wizard list
is marked up as `id="WizardSpells"` — no space. Searching for the visible string
`"Wizard Spells"` finds nothing, which makes the book look like it contains no
wizard spells at all. Sweep for `id="\w*Spell\w*"` to enumerate these sections.
That also surfaces `ArtificerSpellList`, `DunamancySpellList` and warlock
`ExpandedSpellList`s, which must **not** be read as wizard spells.

**Always whitelist the eight schools.** A pattern like "heading followed by
`Nth-level`" also matches class features — "Breath of the Dragon — *3rd-level
feature*" — and invents hundreds of phantom spells. Requiring
`3rd-level evocation` is what separates a spell from a feature.

**Three markup dialects, not two.** Metadata appears as
`<em>Level 3 Evocation (Sorcerer, Wizard)</em>` (2024 books),
`<em>3rd-level evocation</em>`, and
`<p class="Core-Styles_Core-Metadata">8th-level necromancy</p>` (Xanathar's).
Anchor on the `spell-tooltip` heading and accept any of them.

**An illustration can sit between a heading and its metadata**, so search as far
as the next spell heading rather than a fixed character window.

**Normalise case and apostrophes.** Xanathar's lists are sentence case
(`Absorb elements`), PHB 2024 is title case, and curly apostrophes appear in
`Tasha's`. Dedupe on a normalised key and take display names from the listing.

**Exports can be partial.** Several book folders contain only some chapters —
Kwalish's three wizard spells live in its Appendix E. `extract_spells.py`
supports an optional `data/source-overrides.csv` (`Name,Source,Why`) for spells
whose defining chapter isn't available locally. None are needed right now.

---

## What the test suite actually asserts

`crosscheck_books.py` derives wizard spells from the book exports
*independently* of the listing and diffs the two, which is what catches a
truncated scrape. It currently confirms 297 spells across four books (PHB 2024,
Xanathar's, Heroes of Faerûn, Tasha's) with 0 missing and 0 level
disagreements.

Both it and `extract_spells.py` exit with an explicit message when their source
directories are absent. That guard matters: `crosscheck_books.py` passes when
nothing found locally is missing from the listing, so with no books it would
otherwise compare zero spells against zero and print a meaningless `PASS`.

`verify_workbook.py` builds a small workbook from the same formula-generating
code, seeds it with three known wizards, evaluates every formula and asserts the
results — max spell levels, presence detection, `OWNED` / `CAN COPY` /
`TOO HIGH` statuses, per-spell and total costs, the Copy Log rows and log entry,
and the Order of Scribes rate (four level 1–4 spells cost 4 DT normally, 1 DT
for a Scribe, gold unchanged). It also enforces the bounded-`INDEX` rule above.

---

## Before committing a change

- Re-run `make_table_tent.py` with **no** `--url` to reset `build/table-tent.html`
  to a blank placeholder, so an event's form link isn't left in the repo.
  Rendered PDFs keep the link in a link annotation and are gitignored entirely.
- `build/` is committed, so rebuild and re-run both verifiers before pushing:
  a stale workbook in `build/` is worse than none.
